page_note: No cosmological substrate on this page. Entirely a polemical dialogue between the Apostle and a named Nazorean opponent on the question of whether judges are evildoers. The argument proceeds by analogy (earthly judge → God as judge of souls), but it is apologetic argument, not correspondence-mapping cosmos onto cosmos. Both sides reach into the editor's social/legal world (city, tribunal, whip, collar, sword) and into anti-Nazorean controversy. The closing application to "God... a Judge of the souls" who punishes those who "listen to the Devil" is hortatory/polemic apologetic, not substrate teaching. Classify as manichaean_polemic (Nazorean named as interlocutor) interleaved with apostolic_dialogue formulas.
